content: Erythromycin base increases the levels or effects of palovarotene by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. Avoid coadministration of palovarotene with moderate CYP3A inhibitors. If unavoidable, reduce the palovarotene dose by 50%. Erythromycin base decreases the levels or effects of pantothenic acid by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. Erythromycin base increases the levels or effects of parecoxib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Erythromycin base increases the levels or effects of paromomycin by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. Erythromycin base and paroxetine both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. Erythromycin base and pasireotide both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. Erythromycin base and pazopanib both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Erythromycin base increases the levels or effects of pimozide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Erythromycin base increases the levels or effects of pioglitazone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Erythromycin base decreases the effects of piperacillin through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor closely. Bacteriostatic agents may inhibit the effects of bactericidal agents. Ponatinib increases erythromycin base levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. Erythromycin base increases the levels or effects of posaconazole by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Both erythromycin base and posaconazole prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. Erythromycin base increases pravastatin toxicity through OATP1B1 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. OATP1B1 inhibitors may increase the risk of myopathy. Erythromycin base increases the levels or effects of prednisolone by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. Erythromycin base increases the levels or effects of prednisone by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. Pretomanid increases erythromycin base levels through an unspecified mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. Increase monitoring for drug-related adverse effects if pretomanid is coadministered with sensitive OATP1B3 substrates. Erythromycin base increases the levels or effects of propafenone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Erythromycin base decreases the levels or effects of pyridoxine by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. Erythromycin base decreases the levels or effects of pyridoxine (antidote) by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. Quetiapine and erythromycin base both increase the toxicity of each other by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Avoid use with drugs that prolong QT and in patients with risk factors for prolonged QT interval. Postmarketing cases show QT prolongation with overdose in patients with concomitant illness or with drugs known to cause electrolyte imbalance or prolong QT. Erythromycin base increases the levels or effects of quinine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both erythromycin base and quinine prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Quizartinib and erythromycin base both increase the effects of each other by prolonging the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. Monitor patients more frequently with ECG if coadministered with QT-prolonging drugs. Erythromycin base increases the levels or effects of ramelteon by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Erythromycin base and ranolazine both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. Ribociclib increases erythromycin base levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Erythromycin base increases rifaximin levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. Erythromycin base increases rilpivirine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Rilpivirine increases erythromycin base toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Rilpivirine should be used cautiously when coadministered with drugs that have a known risk of Torsades de Pointes. Erythromycin base increases the levels or effects of rimegepant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. Avoid repeating the rimegepant dose within 48 hours if coadministered with a moderate CYP3A4 inhibitor. Erythromycin base increases the levels or effects of risperidone by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Both erythromycin base and risperidone prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. Erythromycin base increases the levels or effects of ritonavir by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. Erythromycin base increases rivaroxaban levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Patients with renal impairment receiving rivaroxaban with drugs that are combined P-gp and weak or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors may have significant increases in exposure compared with patients with normal renal function and no inhibitor use. Since these increases may elevate bleeding risk, use rivaroxaban in this situation only if the potential benefit justifies the potential risk. Erythromycin base increases roflumilast levels through dual inhibition of CYP3A4 and CYP1A2. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. Increased systemic exposure may result in increased adverse reactions. Erythromycin base increases the levels or effects of roflumilast topical by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Erythromycin base increases the levels or effects of romidepsin by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Both erythromycin base and romidepsin prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. Erythromycin base increases rosuvastatin toxicity through OATP1B1 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. OATP1B1 inhibitors may increase the risk of myopathy. Rucaparib increases erythromycin base levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. Adjust the dosage of CYP3A4 substrates if clinically indicated. Erythromycin base increases the levels or effects of ruxolitinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Erythromycin base increases the levels or effects of ruxolitinib topical by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Erythromycin base increases the levels or effects of sacubitril/valsartan through OATP1B1 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. In vitro studies indicate valsartan is a substrate of the hepatic uptake transporter OATP1B1; coadministration with OATP1B1 inhibitors may increase valsartan systemic exposure. Sarecycline increases erythromycin base levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. Monitor for toxicities of P-gp substrates that may require dosage reduction when coadministered with P-gp inhibitors. Erythromycin base increases the levels or effects of saxagliptin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Erythromycin base increases seladelpar levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Exercise caution in patients who are poor CYP2C9 metabolizers taking seladelpar and are coadministered a moderate/strong CYP3A4 inhibitor. Selpercatinib increases erythromycin base toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Erythromycin base increases the levels or effects of sildenafil by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. Consider a starting dose of 25 mg in patients treated with erythromycin. Erythromycin base increases the levels or effects of silodosin by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. Erythromycin base increases the levels or effects of sirolimus by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. Sodium bicarbonate increases erythromycin base levels through an unknown mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. Sodium citrate/citric acid increases erythromycin base levels through an unknown mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. Erythromycin base decreases the effects of sodium picosulfate/magnesium oxide/anhydrous citric acid by altering metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Coadministration with antibiotics decreases efficacy by altering colonic bacterial flora needed to convert sodium picosulfate to its active form. Erythromycin base increases the levels or effects of sonidegib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. Avoid coadministration of sonidegib with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. If a moderate CYP3A inhibitor must be used, administer it for less than 14 days and monitor closely for adverse reactions, particularly musculoskeletal adverse reactions. Sorafenib and erythromycin base both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Erythromycin base increases the levels or effects of sparsentan by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. No dosage adjustment is needed. Monitor blood pressure, serum potassium, edema, and kidney function regularly if sparsentan is coadministered with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. Stiripentol affects erythromycin base metabolism through CYP3A4 inhibition and induction. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. Monitor CYP3A4 substrates coadministered with stiripentol for increased or decreased effects. Stiripentol increases erythromycin base levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. Consider reducing the dose of P-glycoprotein substrates if adverse reactions occur when administered concomitantly with stiripentol. Erythromycin base increases the levels or effects of streptomycin by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. Erythromycin base increases the levels or effects of sufentanil by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Erythromycin base increases the levels or effects of sufentanil SL by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Coadministration of sufentanil SL with any CYP3A4 inhibitor may increase sufentanil plasma concentration, thereby increasing or prolonging adverse effects, including potentially fatal respiratory depression. Sulfamethoxazole and erythromycin base both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. Erythromycin base increases the levels or effects of suvorexant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. Decrease the suvorexant starting dose to 5 mg at bedtime if coadministered with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. Erythromycin base increases the levels or effects of tacrolimus by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. Erythromycin base increases the levels or effects of talazoparib by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. Talazoparib is a P-glycoprotein substrate; coadministration with P-gp inhibitors may increase talazoparib systemic exposure. Erythromycin base affects tamoxifen metabolism by inhibiting CYP3A4, decreasing its conversion to N-desmethyl tamoxifen, an active metabolite with similar biological activity. Use caution and monitor closely. Erythromycin base increases tamsulosin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Dose reduction may be needed for coadministered drugs predominantly metabolized by CYP3A. Tazemetostat decreases erythromycin base levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Tecovirimat decreases erythromycin base levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Tecovirimat is a weak CYP3A4 inducer. Monitor sensitive CYP3A4 substrates for effectiveness if coadministered. Erythromycin base and telavancin both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. Erythromycin base increases the levels or effects of tezacaftor by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. Adjust the tezacaftor dosage regimen if coadministered with a moderate CYP3A inhibitor. Erythromycin base decreases thiamine levels by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. Erythromycin base increases the levels or effects of tinidazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Erythromycin base increases the levels or effects of tobramycin by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. Erythromycin base increases tofacitinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. No specific dose adjustment is recommended when tofacitinib is coadministered with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors; decrease the tofacitinib dose if coadministered with both moderate CYP3A4 and potent CYP2C19 inhibitors. Erythromycin base increases the levels or effects of tolvaptan by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. Erythromycin base increases the levels or effects of trabectedin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Erythromycin base increases the levels or effects of tramadol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. May require decreased tramadol dose or adjustment of dosing interval; increased risk for serious adverse events including seizures and serotonin syndrome. Erythromycin base increases the levels or effects of trazodone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Erythromycin base and trimethoprim both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. Triptorelin increases erythromycin base toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Increases the risk of Torsades de Pointes. Erythromycin base and tropisetron both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required.
